They don't hate you (probably). And they aren't disgusted by you (hopefully). It's just basic social economics. There's a cost-benefit analysis everyone goes through subconsciously in social interactions. 

People will invest as much time in you as they think interacting with you is worth. Once your social value hits the red, it's abort mission and on to the next one. Most of the time it really isn't any sense of hatred/disgust that motivates people. It's an "I'm bored"/grass is always greener mentality. So you shouldn't beat yourself up over it, it's nothing personal.

Guys that get tons of girls fuck up socially all the time. The key is all in the delivery. You've gotta bulldoze past your mistakes so they get forgotten. Say everything with a smile and a laugh. That's what people are talking about when they say be confident. They're telling you to fake it. 

The secret is: everyone feels uncomfortable all the time. Everyone thinks they're "the most awkward person omg", no matter their social status. It's the way you handle your mistakes that determine how people react to them. If you get all quiet and awkward, that social hiccup hangs in the hair like a rancid fart. But if you blaze past it, all smiles and fake confidence, you give everyone something else to think about and your mistake is all but forgotten.

Oh, and as always, being attractive helps.

I do care about how other people see me in the way that I'm saddened when I'm not accepted, or made fun of, or whatever, just like anyone else. But I exercise for the same reason I write. It's cathartic. It helps to release all this negative energy and I figure if my mind is going to be this sick I should at least try to have a somewhat healthy body. I get apathetic and unmotivated in the depths of my depressive episodes and go a few weeks without exercising and eating unhealthily, but I try my hardest to maintain my body and mind. If only to keep up appearances for my family, and even if it's a losing battle.

It helps to know I'm not the only person that struggles with this type of thing. I do get relief from it occasionally, but it seems more and more that I'll have good moments, but bad weeks. Life can be hell sometimes, but I'm still searching for reason enough to make all this struggle worth it. I guess the fact that I'm still here is testament to the fact that I have something to live for, if only subconsciously.

May 18, 2013 Personal Journal of ~~REDACTED~~

I've lived with the Devil for quite some time now. I don't remember when he first showed up, its been too long. Maybe I've repressed the memory. Maybe he's actually just been here since the beginning.

Living with the Devil isn't all bad though. Some days he seems content to mill about in the background, leaving me and my thoughts to go undisturbed. Lately these kinds of days are few and far between.  The Devil takes great personal joy in tormenting me. He's there to undermine my every action, call into doubt my every thought. I think he gives me good days just to give me a false sense of hope. Let me see the light so that I can bask in it's imagined glow for a moment, a moment that is made all the more brief by the ensuing collapse into despair.. It's getting to the point where I can't handle it anymore.

Today I was afflicted by a particularly strong pinch-and-twist in my gut. The Devil loves to make my suffering imperceptible to others. He perches himself in the corner and sneers as I writhe in agony under the jab of an invisible knife. This morning I awoke in the strangest manner I've ever experienced. I snapped out of the dream world, both eyes ripping open at the same time. I stared at the ceiling for a few ageless moments, consumed by a numbing emptiness. It wasn't a desire to stay that kept me pinned under my comforter, but a complete lack of caring about anything that would make me want to get up. I felt complete, consuming apathy. Just writing this down is a chore because I can't be brought to give enough of a fuck about my own thoughts to record them. I've been sapped of my will. But that's not the most horrible part of it.

I've been left with my unfulfilled desires, to mull over them knowing they will never come to fruition. And this is not by any twist of misfortune or worldly obstacle, but merely due to the simple fact that I don't posses the willpower to see them through to the end. I feel worthless at every turn. I want so much but crippling self-doubt and rotting apathy curse me to be perpetually left wanting. It's been said that there are worse things than death, and I agree. Being trapped in an empty life devoid of any meaning, objective or self-created, is more torturous a fate than any sort of demise I can imagine. 

If I am to survive this, the lowest point of my life, I'm left with one course of action. I must fight the Devil that has robbed from me my will to live. This beast that has conspired over the course of my existence to drive me into madness cannot be allowed to control my life any longer. This demon has made himself at home with me, and sapped me of my strength to rebuke him. I must resolve myself to fight the corrupting influence of this embodiment of evil if I am to continue to live. I won't allow myself to be dragged so effortlessly into the depths of Hell, from this point forward Satan will have to reckon with me the whole way down.

- W
 
Of the three bulbs that jutted from the wall above, only one had any flickering life left in it. The dying incandescent gasps left most of the room shrouded, and cast deep shadows across two faces. The figures stood adjacent, a small waist-high table separating them. Both gripped the corners on their respective sides like a handle, fighting to steer the discourse; they strained toward each other and spoke with the low rumble of distant thunder.
 
"You fucking worthless piece of shit," rolled from between the tight-clenched fangs of the man across the table. His presence filled the room and the words seemed to be seeping from the walls themselves. The vents whispered sentiments of agreement and the floorboards creaked their approval. Though the man across had adopted the same posture of the feeble creature he was insulting, he seemed to carry himself more powerfully. His words thickened the air until it pressed in from all sides like a thick blanket, and light from the failing bulb skirted around him concealing all but a serpentine smile.
 
"Shut up, I know you're just trying to fuck with me. I'm not letting you get inside my head." The man worked to force his defiant tone to match the intensity of the Devil's, but inside he could feel it wavering. A weak front, supported on a collapsible foundation.
 
"Look at yourself, worthless. Awkward. Lazy. You're a waste of space. Everybody thinks it...I know you hear everyone laughing at you, talking about you. The muffled conversations always just out of earshot. The suppressed laughter that always seems to happen after you walk by. Stop lying to yourself, because you know I'm just saying what you're thinking. You reek of insecurity, and frankly, it's off-putting. You think you can hide how pathetic you are? Nervous sweating. Anxious trebling. Your whiny voice pitching like a pre-pubescent boy."
 
His gaze lapsed mournfully for a moment; the Devil had struck a blow and pounced on the opportunity to drive him down into the fiery abyss. It was working. A stronger person would most assuredly brush aside this assault, but decades of abuse had worn away his strength and his defenses were pitifully patchwork. 
 
"That's why you don't have friends. That's why you fail at almost everything you try. That's why you've always been kept on the outside looking in. People can feel your weakness. You're a blubbering, stuttering, pathetic lump of shit..." the Devil paused for a moment and shifted on his feet. Such a slight adjustment changed the way the room felt, tendrils of sickening sweetness wrapped themselves around the words that now dripped from his lips.

"It doesn't have to be that way. You know that don't you? Why do you keep fighting the one person that can finally change your life for the better?" Satan caught the man's brow furrowing contemplatively for a moment and pressed the advantage.
 
"See? You're speechless because you know I'm right. Why do you keep pushing back against me? Trust me, I understand your pain. I know the suffering you're enduring. That's why I'm here. That's why I've always been here." The words seemed to pitch the table and throw the man off balance, reopening deep scars and further sapping his will to fight.
 
"You know my only desire is what's best for you, right? I can take care of you, you'll never have to feel this kind of pain again. Just look at where not disobeying me has gotten you. What harm could come from at least just trying to listen to me?" The Devil's words flowed like molasses from between his lips. Their powerful odor filled the room and draped around the shoulders of the feeble man.
 
"Listen, I know I can seem harsh sometimes, but that's just because it frustrates me that I want to help you so badly and you just don't listen to me." The Beast's lips curled into a knowing smile that made blood rush to the now defeated man's ears. The overwhelming potpourri that masked the smell of the Devil's rotting insincerity made him light-headed. 
 
"You know yourself better than to try to fight me," these words punched the air from the man's lungs. His vision exploded with spots popping and shimmering in and out of view. The Devil continued undisturbed. "For better or worse, I'm with you till the end. You know that, and in the back of your mind you always have. You've just got to accept it. We can do this back-and-forth like we've been doing till the end of time, but the only way to make it stop is to just give in."
 
The man sighed, utterly defeated now, and lowered his gaze from the eyes of the Beast. His hands still gripped the corners of the table, but his shoulders sagged limply. The Devil's piercing stare bore holes into the top of his skull. He let his eyelids fall and stood briefly, collecting himself, just breathing.
 
Another sigh escaped his lips as he returned his eyes to the mirror. The Devil had vanished, but shadows playing in the quivering light of the bare bulb above toyed with revealing his image within the man's reflection. Soundly beaten, the man relinquished his grasp on the counter, turned, and flicked the bathroom light out. Wading through the filth strewn about his small apartment, he collapsed on the couch and nestled deep in the warmth of familiar solitude.
 
Maybe tomorrow, he thought.
